abilities.name: Arcane Crepuscular
unmodeled_effects: Invisibility is not simulated: ticking this treats the wielder as invisible for the whole fight.
Its +30% Ability Strength is not applied to the buffs here; add it to the Ability Strength box if it should be.

abilities.name: Energized Munitions
unmodeled_effects: Its Energy cost is not modelled: 50 Energy for 5 s at 100% Ability Duration, and this fight has no energy economy. Set the duration to what your build keeps up.
Its reserve refill adds nothing here: reserves are infinite by default. Its effect on how often you reload is modelled.

abilities.name: Resupply
unmodeled_effects: The pack refills the magazine instantly. Reserves are infinite by default, so the refill adds nothing here, and running the pack dry is not simulated.
Arch-guns and battery weapons (Kitguns with Pax Charge included) get nothing from it in game. The sim does not exclude them, so on those weapons it reads high.

abilities.name: Tenacious Bond
unmodeled_effects: The condition, the companion's critical chance over 50%, is not checked: ticking this treats it as met.
Headshot kills shorten the companion's recovery timer. There is no companion to revive here; the number is unaffected.

abilities.name: Toxic Lash
unmodeled_effects: The card doubles this on melee strikes; the sim fires guns, so only the gun half applies.
Contagion Cloud, its augment, leaves a damaging cloud where an enemy dies. It needs a corpse and a second target, so it is not counted; against a crowd the number reads low.

abilities.name: Wrathful Advance
unmodeled_effects: The teleport and its heavy attack are not modelled: the ability swaps to melee and strikes the target it jumps to. Only the buff the cast leaves behind is modelled.
Kullervo's passive, +75% Heavy Attack Efficiency and +100% Heavy Attack Wind Up speed, belongs to the Warframe, and this fight has no Warframe.

abilities.name: Wrathful Advance (Helminth)
unmodeled_effects: The teleport and its heavy attack are not modelled: the ability swaps to melee and strikes the target it jumps to. Only the buff the cast leaves behind is modelled.
Kullervo's passive, +75% Heavy Attack Efficiency and +100% Heavy Attack Wind Up speed, belongs to the Warframe, and this fight has no Warframe.

live_bugs: An extra hit also fires off a Blast detonation, taking the faction bonus a third time and the elemental bonus the detonation itself is denied. The wiki lists it as a bug; it is modelled as it plays now, and a fix would change this number.
abilities.name: Xata's Whisper
unmodeled_effects: The Bullet Attractor deals no damage. Its value, redirecting enemy fire and letting a punch-through round hit twice, needs enemies that shoot back and a second target; the number is unaffected.
The Void proc's reset of Sentient and Shadow Stalker damage adaptation is not modelled.
The Vast Untime's +50% Void vulnerability, and its pause on this buff's timer, belong to another Xaku ability, which is not modelled.
Whether a lingering field's tick (the Torid's cloud) triggers an extra hit is stated by neither wiki, so it does not here.
Its own crit roll — 0% base, 1x, raised only by headshot crit chance (Covenant, a charged Concentrated Arrow) — is not modelled; with neither in the build it never crits of its own.
A sneak attack on the hit is not copied onto it; the sim has no sneak attacks.

benchmarks.name: Standard Single Target · Thrax Centurion Lv 9999 SP · 100% headshots, aiming · 180 s · KPM
rules: The target is one Thrax Centurion at level 9999 on Steel Path. The fight lasts 180 seconds.

The target is a Thrax Centurion because a build that beats it transfers: it belongs to no faction, so no faction mod and no faction bonus reads on it; it carries Overguard, which most Warframe abilities cannot take off, so the weapon has to; it is armoured and tanky; it is immune to no element, so every proc lands; its weak points are the ordinary ones, 3x on the head and 1x elsewhere.
Its flaws are stated rather than hidden: it carries no shield, its Overguard may sit high, and the spectral form it enters on death is switched off here.
One target: damage that reaches other enemies counts for nothing here.
Shots are aimed, with a 100% headshot rate. A weapon's forced targeting and stance still apply.
The score is kills per minute, counting the fraction of the current target already gone. Removing 3% of one target in 180 seconds scores 0.03 and still ranks.

Every main slot is filled, every evolution tier the entry has is taken, every arcane seat it has is filled. The Exilus slot is optional: a row may wear one and a row without one is not a lesser build, so the two sit on the same board and the better number wins.

The stance slot is optional too, and it is not a discount but a GRANT: a stance hands the weapon 10 mod capacity on a matching polarity, 5 on a bare slot and 4 on the wrong colour. A row without one is not a lesser build; it is a build that spent the capacity elsewhere.
Investment is not ranked: every entry is scored at full Forma, at max rank, and at the maximum roll of any bonus a player can raise by farming duplicates.
The reserve is not spent: every entry fires as if it were being resupplied, so nothing here ranks ammo economy. An entry that cannot be resupplied at all runs on its own reserve.

The melee weapon is DRAWN, not quick-melee: a card that says "With Melee Weapon Equipped" pays here. A build swung out of a gun is a different fight and the simulator has a switch for it; the ruler does not.
An entry that can be played more than one way is ranked once per way, and the way it was played is part of the row.

A buff starts the fight FULL only if it is permanent — no timer, and not spent by being used. Such a buff can be held for the whole fight by anyone, so scoring it at anything less would rank how long ago the entrant last topped it up. Every other buff starts at zero and is earned in the fight. Two buffs in the data qualify today.
Nobody submits a number. A submission is a BUILD, and its score is computed here by this engine under the pinned seed above, so any row can be reproduced exactly by anyone with the repo.
benchmarks.standard: Standard means one set of conditions for every build: one tough, unaffiliated target, the same fight and the same rules, so a number reproduces on any machine and any two builds compare directly. Your own conditions are set in the simulator.

The target is a Thrax Centurion because a build that beats it transfers: it belongs to no faction, so no faction mod and no faction bonus reads on it; it carries Overguard, which most Warframe abilities cannot take off, so the weapon has to; it is armoured and tanky; it is immune to no element, so every proc lands; its weak points are the ordinary ones, 3x on the head and 1x elsewhere.
Its flaws are stated rather than hidden: it carries no shield, its Overguard may sit high, and the spectral form it enters on death is switched off here.
One target: damage that reaches other enemies counts for nothing here.
Shots are aimed, with a 50% headshot rate. A weapon's forced targeting and stance still apply.
The score is kills per minute, counting the fraction of the current target already gone. Removing 3% of one target in 180 seconds scores 0.03 and still ranks.

Every main slot is filled, every evolution tier the entry has is taken, every arcane seat it has is filled. The Exilus slot is optional: a row may wear one and a row without one is not a lesser build, so the two sit on the same board and the better number wins.

The stance slot is optional too, and it is not a discount but a GRANT: a stance hands the weapon 10 mod capacity on a matching polarity, 5 on a bare slot and 4 on the wrong colour. A row without one is not a lesser build; it is a build that spent the capacity elsewhere.
Investment is not ranked: every entry is scored at full Forma, at max rank, and at the maximum roll of any bonus a player can raise by farming duplicates.
The reserve is not spent: every entry fires as if it were being resupplied, so nothing here ranks ammo economy. An entry that cannot be resupplied at all runs on its own reserve.

The melee weapon is DRAWN, not quick-melee: a card that says "With Melee Weapon Equipped" pays here. A build swung out of a gun is a different fight and the simulator has a switch for it; the ruler does not.
An entry that can be played more than one way is ranked once per way, and the way it was played is part of the row.

A buff starts the fight FULL only if it is permanent — no timer, and not spent by being used. Such a buff can be held for the whole fight by anyone, so scoring it at anything less would rank how long ago the entrant last topped it up. Every other buff starts at zero and is earned in the fight. Two buffs in the data qualify today.
Nobody submits a number. A submission is a BUILD, and its score is computed here by this engine under the pinned seed above, so any row can be reproduced exactly by anyone with the repo.
benchmarks.standard: Standard means one set of conditions for every build: one tough, unaffiliated target, the same fight and the same rules, so a number reproduces on any machine and any two builds compare directly. Your own conditions are set in the simulator.

benchmarks.name: Standard Multi Target · 5x5 at 3 m · Thrax Centurion Lv 9999 SP · 100% headshots, aiming · 180 s · KPM
rules: The target is a formation of 25 Thrax Centurions at level 9999 on Steel Path, a 5 by 5 grid spaced 3 metres centre to centre: the smallest odd square that holds every elemental area effect around the aimed body whole, a fully grown 6 m Gas cloud included. The fight lasts 180 seconds.
A weapon's own explosion wider than about 6 m, and punch-through past five bodies, are clipped by the grid on purpose: a deeper column would rank the formation rather than the weapon.
The spacing decides whether splash or single-target damage wins: 3 m is where that ordering matches play, and it is the widest whole metre at which Electricity still reaches a neighbour.

The target is a Thrax Centurion because a build that beats it transfers: it belongs to no faction, so no faction mod and no faction bonus reads on it; it carries Overguard, which most Warframe abilities cannot take off, so the weapon has to; it is armoured and tanky; it is immune to no element, so every proc lands; its weak points are the ordinary ones, 3x on the head and 1x elsewhere.
The shooter stands at contact with the middle body of the front rank, and fires along the line that rank faces.
Shots are aimed, with a 100% headshot rate. A weapon's forced targeting and stance still apply.

Direct hits, including punch-through hits, use the selected headshot rate. A chain hop and a damage cloud cannot be a weak point hit. A Blast detonation carries the weak-point and critical multipliers of the hit that applied the stack (MEASUREMENTS M54).
The score is kills per minute across the whole formation, counting the fraction of each target already gone.
A body that dies respawns where it stood, so the arrangement is the same at the end as at the start and the score is a rate rather than a race to the last body.
The grid is stated as three numbers rather than as 25 positions, so its terms can be read and argued with.

An entry that can be played more than one way is ranked once per way, and the way it was played is part of the row.

A buff starts the fight FULL only if it is permanent — no timer, and not spent by being used. Such a buff can be held for the whole fight by anyone, so scoring it at anything less would rank how long ago the entrant last topped it up. Every other buff starts at zero and is earned in the fight. Two buffs in the data qualify today.
Nobody submits a number. A submission is a BUILD, and its score is computed here by this engine under the pinned seed above, so any row can be reproduced exactly by anyone with the repo.
benchmarks.standard: One specific fight players run, measured as it is rather than as a stand-in for most play: the Eximus Corrupted Heavy Gunner of the Void Fissures, taken apart by one weapon.

method.about: How WFSim judges a Warframe build: each rule is what the calculator does, why it does it, and the readings it rests on.

apply: Before comparing two builds, check that both were scored under the same ruler; under different rulers, do not compare the numbers.
Quote a score together with the name of its ruler.

evidence.shows: The same Void instance reads 14 on a Thrax Centurion's body and 9 on another unit's body.

concepts.rule: A build is judged in a named fight, its ruler, which states the target, its level, how long the fight lasts and what is counted, and a score compares only with scores under the same ruler.
concepts.title: A score belongs to its ruler
why: What a hit is worth depends on what it hits: armour, Overguard, faction, elemental weakness and how many bodies stand in reach each change it. A number without its fight cannot be reproduced or compared.
A ruler states every term, so anyone can run the same fight and get the same score.
The best build under one ruler can differ from the best under another; that is the fight answering a different question.

apply: Do not credit a timed or on-kill buff at full stacks against a tough target; ask how often the build earns it there.
A build that leads against weak targets can trail against tough ones, and the reverse.

evidence.shows: One build scored 60% lower against a level 9999 Steel Path target when its timed buffs started at zero and had to be earned, and 0.9% lower at level 30.

concepts.rule: Under a ruler, stacks, buffs, status effects, Overguard and armour start where the game starts them and change hit by hit during the fight; nothing starts at its cap because a card allows one.
concepts.title: The fight is run, not assumed
why: A buff that stacks on kills is worth what the fight lets it earn. Against a target that dies twice a minute it is rarely earned; against one that dies every second it is held almost all the time.
Each hit lands on what the hits before it left: a status already on the target, armour already stripped, a pile about to detonate.
Only a buff with no timer that nothing spends starts full, because anyone can hold it for the whole fight.

apply: Judge a build by its kills per minute under a ruler, not by its damage per second.
Do not count multishot as extra rounds reaching other targets.

evidence.shows: A three-round burst at a body that dies to one round kills that body, and nothing of the burst reaches the body behind it.
A shot that brings a Blast pile to ten detonates it once, and the rest of that shot's Blast procs are lost.

concepts.rule: A ruler counts kills per minute, including the part of a target already gone, so damage that reaches a body already dead, or a pile already full, adds nothing.
concepts.title: Kills per minute, not damage per second
why: Damage per second counts every number a weapon deals, including damage on a body already dead. Kills per minute counts only what removes targets.
Multishot adds instances to the weapon's own rounds: each its own number, crit and status, landing where the round lands.
Counting the part of a target already gone lets a build that never finishes a kill still rank.

apply: Where a card's wording and a reading in the game disagree, follow the reading.
Where your own reading in the game disagrees with WFSim, yours is the one to trust.

evidence.shows: Headshot bonuses of +50% and +30% read 1.1998 times the first in game: they add (1.2), they do not multiply (1.3).
A throw reloads after every throw, so its cycle is the wind-up plus the reload, 1.6 s rather than the 1 s its fire rate suggests.

concepts.rule: Where a reading taken in the game, the wiki and DE's public export disagree, the reading wins, then the wiki, then the export; every formula in the engine names its source.
concepts.title: The game is the authority
why: A card's text and the wiki describe the game, and they can leave out how two effects combine or what a listed number means. A reading in the game settles it.
Each reading the engine applies is published with its numbers, so anyone can take it again.
A tested value changes only with a new reading in the game.

apply: Do not rank builds from a single trial.
Link to a board row rather than restating it: the link opens the build in the calculator, where it can be run again.

evidence.shows: One run per candidate put a status mod at +30% give or take 39 points; four hundred runs still left it give or take 5.6.

concepts.rule: A board build is one anyone submitted or a search found, and its score is the engine's: the ruler's fight run many times under a pinned seed.
concepts.title: A score is computed, never typed
why: Chance decides much of what a build does, so one trial cannot rank it: one run's spread can put a minus sign in front of a status mod worth +30%.
A pinned seed makes every score reproducible by anyone with the source.
A submission is a build, never a number, so no score on the board was typed in.

apply: Quote the riven-free row as what a weapon does, and a riven row as what that shape adds to it.
Compare rivens by their gain over the riven-free leader of the same ruler and mode.
concepts.rule: The board leads with the best build that has no riven; a riven is ranked as a shape, which stats it rolled and which is the malus, scored at its best roll beside the riven-free leader.

see.shows: How the board stores and ranks a riven shape.

concepts.title: The weapon first, without a riven
why: A riven is one player's random item, and ranking items would rank luck. A shape is something anyone can roll for.
Every build is scored at full investment: full Forma, every card at max rank, the maximum Valence bonus. The board ranks choices, not how much someone farmed.

apply: Carry a weapon's notes on what is not modelled along with its score.
Where a gap bears on the question, say so instead of estimating around it.
concepts.rule: A weapon, a mod, an arcane, an evolution and an enemy each state what the engine does not model of them, and a score holds only inside what is modelled.

see.shows: Every mechanic the engine does not model, in one register.

concepts.title: What is not modelled is said
why: A number with a gap nobody stated reads as complete. A stated gap says where to check the game yourself.

A glaive bounces off the bodies it cannot punch through: the body it was thrown into is its first bounce, and the last its count allows turns it for home. With no walls here, a glaive that passes every body flies its whole range and bounces off nothing. A quick throw is given the charged throw's count, the only one published, and the flight between bounces adds no time.

A bounce explosion (Volatile Rebound, Volatile Quick Return) takes no combo multiplier and spends no combo (wiki); whether Killing Blow or any other heavy-attack card reaches it is unpublished, and here none does. Volatile Quick Return's +3 Blast Radius is put on the bounce explosion alone.
A detonated glaive goes off on its way out, no further than the first body it cannot pass, and makes no bounce after that one: the fight does not wait for the bounces it could still have made.
How fast a thrown glaive comes back is unpublished: one left to return is taken to fly back over the same distance at its own speed, and a detonated one is in the hand at once.
A throw's own animation is unpublished: it is taken as one attack at the throw's listed rate, after the charge where there is one, and attack speed shortens it.
Tennokai on a throw is not modelled as the game has it: the window pauses while the glaive flies and only a detonation spends it.
Melee Animosity counts a throw as a heavy attack that pays its bonus and spends no stack; here a throw is a light input.
On a throw the innate Toxin never combines with modded elements (wiki); here it combines as on a swing.

A glaive bounces off the bodies it cannot punch through: the body it was thrown into is its first bounce, and the last its count allows turns it for home. With no walls here, a glaive that passes every body flies its whole range and bounces off nothing. A quick throw is given the charged throw's count, the only one published, and the flight between bounces adds no time.

A bounce explosion (Volatile Rebound, Volatile Quick Return) takes no combo multiplier and spends no combo (wiki); whether Killing Blow or any other heavy-attack card reaches it is unpublished, and here none does. Volatile Quick Return's +3 Blast Radius is put on the bounce explosion alone.
A detonated glaive goes off on its way out, no further than the first body it cannot pass, and makes no bounce after that one: the fight does not wait for the bounces it could still have made.
How fast a thrown glaive comes back is unpublished: one left to return is taken to fly back over the same distance at its own speed, and a detonated one is in the hand at once.
A throw's own animation is unpublished: it is taken as one attack at the throw's listed rate, after the charge where there is one, and attack speed shortens it.
Tennokai on a throw is not modelled as the game has it: the window pauses while the glaive flies and only a detonation spends it.
Melee Animosity counts a throw as a heavy attack that pays its bonus and spends no stack; here a throw is a light input.
The Maggots a throw drops are not modelled: the page gives no damage and no radius for them.
The Throw Recall Explosion's 12% crit chance is the module's, against 22% on every other quick-throw row; unmeasured.

A glaive bounces off the bodies it cannot punch through: the body it was thrown into is its first bounce, and the last its count allows turns it for home. With no walls here, a glaive that passes every body flies its whole range and bounces off nothing. A quick throw is given the charged throw's count, the only one published, and the flight between bounces adds no time.

A bounce explosion (Volatile Rebound, Volatile Quick Return) takes no combo multiplier and spends no combo (wiki); whether Killing Blow or any other heavy-attack card reaches it is unpublished, and here none does. Volatile Quick Return's +3 Blast Radius is put on the bounce explosion alone.
A detonated glaive goes off on its way out, no further than the first body it cannot pass, and makes no bounce after that one: the fight does not wait for the bounces it could still have made.
How fast a thrown glaive comes back is unpublished: one left to return is taken to fly back over the same distance at its own speed, and a detonated one is in the hand at once.
A throw's own animation is unpublished: it is taken as one attack at the throw's listed rate, after the charge where there is one, and attack speed shortens it.
Tennokai on a throw is not modelled as the game has it: the window pauses while the glaive flies and only a detonation spends it.
Melee Animosity counts a throw as a heavy attack that pays its bonus and spends no stack; here a throw is a light input.

A glaive's heavy attack is the detonation of a thrown glaive, which is its own mode (a throw, detonated), so there is no standing heavy mode and a Tennokai window converts no swing.

A glaive bounces off the bodies it cannot punch through: the body it was thrown into is its first bounce, and the last its count allows turns it for home. With no walls here, a glaive that passes every body flies its whole range and bounces off nothing. A quick throw is given the charged throw's count, the only one published, and the flight between bounces adds no time.

A bounce explosion (Volatile Rebound, Volatile Quick Return) takes no combo multiplier and spends no combo (wiki); whether Killing Blow or any other heavy-attack card reaches it is unpublished, and here none does. Volatile Quick Return's +3 Blast Radius is put on the bounce explosion alone.
A detonated glaive goes off on its way out, no further than the first body it cannot pass, and makes no bounce after that one: the fight does not wait for the bounces it could still have made.
How fast a thrown glaive comes back is unpublished: one left to return is taken to fly back over the same distance at its own speed, and a detonated one is in the hand at once.
A throw's own animation is unpublished: it is taken as one attack at the throw's listed rate, after the charge where there is one, and attack speed shortens it.
Tennokai on a throw is not modelled as the game has it: the window pauses while the glaive flies and only a detonation spends it.
Melee Animosity counts a throw as a heavy attack that pays its bonus and spends no stack; here a throw is a light input.
The quick throw's 450 Blast detonation is the module's, the same as its bounce explosion where every other glaive doubles it; unmeasured.
A throw's 50% chance to disarm is not modelled; nothing here is armed.

The climb is not timed: this loop takes the 150% radius of a slam dropped from 15 m and spends no time getting up there. A player who hops instead gets less radius, down to the 2.5 m / listed floor; this fight has no vertical axis to tell the two apart.
A glaive's heavy attack is the detonation of a thrown glaive, which is its own mode (a throw, detonated), so there is no standing heavy mode and a Tennokai window converts no swing.

A glaive bounces off the bodies it cannot punch through: the body it was thrown into is its first bounce, and the last its count allows turns it for home. With no walls here, a glaive that passes every body flies its whole range and bounces off nothing. A quick throw is given the charged throw's count, the only one published, and the flight between bounces adds no time.

A bounce explosion (Volatile Rebound, Volatile Quick Return) takes no combo multiplier and spends no combo (wiki); whether Killing Blow or any other heavy-attack card reaches it is unpublished, and here none does. Volatile Quick Return's +3 Blast Radius is put on the bounce explosion alone.
A detonated glaive goes off on its way out, no further than the first body it cannot pass, and makes no bounce after that one: the fight does not wait for the bounces it could still have made.
How fast a thrown glaive comes back is unpublished: one left to return is taken to fly back over the same distance at its own speed, and a detonated one is in the hand at once.
A throw's own animation is unpublished: it is taken as one attack at the throw's listed rate, after the charge where there is one, and attack speed shortens it.
Tennokai on a throw is not modelled as the game has it: the window pauses while the glaive flies and only a detonation spends it.
Melee Animosity counts a throw as a heavy attack that pays its bonus and spends no stack; here a throw is a light input.
A throw's 50% chance to disarm is not modelled; nothing here is armed.

A glaive bounces off the bodies it cannot punch through: the body it was thrown into is its first bounce, and the last its count allows turns it for home. With no walls here, a glaive that passes every body flies its whole range and bounces off nothing. A quick throw is given the charged throw's count, the only one published, and the flight between bounces adds no time.

A bounce explosion (Volatile Rebound, Volatile Quick Return) takes no combo multiplier and spends no combo (wiki); whether Killing Blow or any other heavy-attack card reaches it is unpublished, and here none does. Volatile Quick Return's +3 Blast Radius is put on the bounce explosion alone.
A detonated glaive goes off on its way out, no further than the first body it cannot pass, and makes no bounce after that one: the fight does not wait for the bounces it could still have made.
How fast a thrown glaive comes back is unpublished: one left to return is taken to fly back over the same distance at its own speed, and a detonated one is in the hand at once.
A throw's own animation is unpublished: it is taken as one attack at the throw's listed rate, after the charge where there is one, and attack speed shortens it.
Tennokai on a throw is not modelled as the game has it: the window pauses while the glaive flies and only a detonation spends it.
Melee Animosity counts a throw as a heavy attack that pays its bonus and spends no stack; here a throw is a light input.
The detonation's 40% falloff and 3.6 m are the page's; the module states no falloff, and 4 m on the charged throw. Unmeasured.
The throw forces Ragdoll (the module's ForcedProcs), a state this arena does not have.

A glaive bounces off the bodies it cannot punch through: the body it was thrown into is its first bounce, and the last its count allows turns it for home. With no walls here, a glaive that passes every body flies its whole range and bounces off nothing. A quick throw is given the charged throw's count, the only one published, and the flight between bounces adds no time.

A bounce explosion (Volatile Rebound, Volatile Quick Return) takes no combo multiplier and spends no combo (wiki); whether Killing Blow or any other heavy-attack card reaches it is unpublished, and here none does. Volatile Quick Return's +3 Blast Radius is put on the bounce explosion alone.
A detonated glaive goes off on its way out, no further than the first body it cannot pass, and makes no bounce after that one: the fight does not wait for the bounces it could still have made.
How fast a thrown glaive comes back is unpublished: one left to return is taken to fly back over the same distance at its own speed, and a detonated one is in the hand at once.
A throw's own animation is unpublished: it is taken as one attack at the throw's listed rate, after the charge where there is one, and attack speed shortens it.
Tennokai on a throw is not modelled as the game has it: the window pauses while the glaive flies and only a detonation spends it.
Melee Animosity counts a throw as a heavy attack that pays its bonus and spends no stack; here a throw is a light input.
The glaive seeks enemies by itself (wiki, Volatile Rebound); here it flies straight and bounces where reflection takes it.

A glaive bounces off the bodies it cannot punch through: the body it was thrown into is its first bounce, and the last its count allows turns it for home. With no walls here, a glaive that passes every body flies its whole range and bounces off nothing. A quick throw is given the charged throw's count, the only one published, and the flight between bounces adds no time.

A bounce explosion (Volatile Rebound, Volatile Quick Return) takes no combo multiplier and spends no combo (wiki); whether Killing Blow or any other heavy-attack card reaches it is unpublished, and here none does. Volatile Quick Return's +3 Blast Radius is put on the bounce explosion alone.
A detonated glaive goes off on its way out, no further than the first body it cannot pass, and makes no bounce after that one: the fight does not wait for the bounces it could still have made.
How fast a thrown glaive comes back is unpublished: one left to return is taken to fly back over the same distance at its own speed, and a detonated one is in the hand at once.
A throw's own animation is unpublished: it is taken as one attack at the throw's listed rate, after the charge where there is one, and attack speed shortens it.
Tennokai on a throw is not modelled as the game has it: the window pauses while the glaive flies and only a detonation spends it.
Melee Animosity counts a throw as a heavy attack that pays its bonus and spends no stack; here a throw is a light input.

A glaive bounces off the bodies it cannot punch through: the body it was thrown into is its first bounce, and the last its count allows turns it for home. With no walls here, a glaive that passes every body flies its whole range and bounces off nothing. A quick throw is given the charged throw's count, the only one published, and the flight between bounces adds no time.

A bounce explosion (Volatile Rebound, Volatile Quick Return) takes no combo multiplier and spends no combo (wiki); whether Killing Blow or any other heavy-attack card reaches it is unpublished, and here none does. Volatile Quick Return's +3 Blast Radius is put on the bounce explosion alone.
A detonated glaive goes off on its way out, no further than the first body it cannot pass, and makes no bounce after that one: the fight does not wait for the bounces it could still have made.
How fast a thrown glaive comes back is unpublished: one left to return is taken to fly back over the same distance at its own speed, and a detonated one is in the hand at once.
A throw's own animation is unpublished: it is taken as one attack at the throw's listed rate, after the charge where there is one, and attack speed shortens it.
Tennokai on a throw is not modelled as the game has it: the window pauses while the glaive flies and only a detonation spends it.
Melee Animosity counts a throw as a heavy attack that pays its bonus and spends no stack; here a throw is a light input.
The Charged Throw's direct damage is the module's, the same as the quick throw's where every other glaive doubles it; unmeasured.

It is 1.5 s of draw for 1,000 damage (500 Cold, 250 Puncture, 250 Slash) at 36% crit, 3.0x, 36% status and 2 m punch through, against this draw's 400 at 32% and 2.4x. unmodeled: The explosion is the whole weapon, and its radius is not modelled: the mine deals no contact damage, so this entry carries the blast as the shot's own damage. Against one target, as in this fight and on the boards, the number is exact; against a crowd it reads low.

The mines are detonated by hand with the alt-fire, and several can be laid first (wiki). The sim detonates each on landing: the ceiling for one mine. Laying several and detonating them together is not modelled.
Mines stick to surfaces, enemies and allies, and multishot throws them in a very wide horizontal spread (wiki), so on this weapon multishot covers ground rather than adding damage to one target.
The Purity syndicate effect heals and cleanses the wielder and nearby allies (wiki). There is no health and no ally here; the number is unaffected.
This weapon is silent; there is nobody to alert here, so stealth is worth nothing.
The blast needs no line of sight. There is no cover here, so the perk adds nothing.
